answer: Each agent resists Sybils via sequential commitment: start from public lotus seed mixed with latest ledger hash, compute 16384 successive SHA-256 hashes ending with unique walnut nonce. Shared sequential verifier processes one chain at a time. Round count (shale-hardness) rises by 256 every 10 new identities, so k-th clone costs more sequential time. Farms cannot batch as each chain depends on prior hash and queues for verification; identity count becomes cumulative wall-clock delay on shared clock, not parallel work.
